## The C.R.E.A.T.E. method

- Hoskins, S. G., Stevens, L. M. & Nehm, R. H. (2007). Selective use of the primary literature transforms the classroom into a virtual laboratory. *Genetics* 176(3), 1381–1389. <https://doi.org/10.1534/genetics.107.071183>
- Hoskins, S. G., Lopatto, D. & Stevens, L. M. (2011). The C.R.E.A.T.E. approach to primary literature shifts undergraduates' self-assessed ability to read and analyze journal articles, attitudes about science, and epistemological beliefs. *CBE—Life Sciences Education* 10(4), 368–378. <https://doi.org/10.1187/cbe.11-03-0027>
- C.R.E.A.T.E. (Consider, Read, Elucidate hypotheses, Analyze and interpret the data, Think of the next Experiment) resources: <https://teachcreate.org>

## Reference quality control

Verified against published records during the site review: the anchor-article titles, the Huang et al. author list and DOI, the Cecilio et al. DOI and species (*P. duboscqi*, *L. major*), the Hoskins et al. (2007) title, volume and first page, the Hoskins et al. (2011) title, the Shigematsu et al. (2003) title, journal and DOI, and *The Delftia Book* authorship. Not independently confirmed (check before publication): the Cecilio et al. article number (16:3571, taken from the course documents), the Hoskins et al. DOIs and the 2011 volume and pages, end pages for Wen et al. (1999), Hoskins et al. (2007) and Shigematsu et al. (2003), and the live status of the WHO and teachcreate.org links.
